notes.name: Auth tokens and refresh rotation
notes.description: How access and refresh tokens are issued, stored and rotated in the API
notes.snippet: Access tokens are short lived (15 minutes) and signed with RS256. The refresh token lives in an httpOnly cookie and is rotated on every use: presenting an already-used refresh token revokes the whole family, which is what catches a stolen cookie being replayed from a second machine. ## Why rotation

notes.name: Zero downtime database migrations
notes.description: Expand and contract migration pattern, and the rule about dropping columns
notes.snippet: Every schema change is expand-then-contract. Add the new column, backfill it, start writing to both, switch reads, and only then drop the old one, in a separate release, never the same one. ## The rule about dropping A column is never dropped in the release that stops using it. notes.name: Observability standards
notes.description: Logs, metrics and dashboards, what we keep and why
notes.snippet: ## Logs Metrics are cheap to add and expensive to keep. Every counter that nobody reads still costs storage, still shows up in the dashboard picker, and still has to be migrated when the backend changes. notes.name: Rate limiting at the edge
notes.description: Token bucket per API key, and why the limit lives at the edge and not in the app
notes.snippet: Rate limiting runs in the edge worker, not in the application. A limiter inside the app still pays for connection setup and a database round trip before it says no, so an abusive client costs almost as much when blocked as when served. ## The bucket Token bucket, 100 requests per minute per API key,

notes.name: Measure before fixing
notes.description: A quality change without a measurement is a guess dressed as work
notes.snippet: Do not change something for quality without an instrument that would show the change failing. The instrument comes first, and the case that fails goes into it before the fix, not after. ## Why it generalises This applies to code, to writing and to process. notes.name: Conference talk on incident reviews
notes.description: Outline of the talk about blameless incident reviews and what the audience asked
notes.snippet: The talk argues that an incident review which produces a list of individual mistakes has failed, because the next person will make a different mistake in the same gap. ## What the audience asked Every single time, someone asks how to run this when a customer is demanding to know who is responsible.

notes.description: The four interviews, what each one is for, and the rejection reasons that repeat
notes.snippet: Four interviews: a screen, a systems design session, a code reading exercise and a values conversation. notes.description: The three steps of checkout, and where customers actually drop off
notes.snippet: Checkout is three steps: cart review, shipping address, payment. notes.name: Form validation rules
notes.description: Client validation mirrors the server, and never replaces it
notes.snippet: Client-side validation exists to give fast feedback. The server validates again, always, because the client is not a trust boundary. ## Error copy Errors name the field and say what to do, never just invalid.
